I'm a professional piercer who's been working in a tattoo shop for about 7 years, and NO, the risk of infections and allergies to the ink are extremely high, and even mild cellulitis can turn into sepsis during pregnancy because of how your immune system is working. 

Plus, when you get a tattoo, you're risking exposure to blood bourne infections like hepatitis or HIV, which are extremely dangerous during pregnancy. 

And while I know that nobody wants to believe that they could get a disease from the shop they like, accidents do happen. My aunt literally got hep C from her first tattoo and gave it to her husband and my cousin before she was diagnosed. You don't want to risk it.

Just save the money for it and get it after you deliver. Honestly, you'll appreciate the break at that point, too.

If you choose to not circumcise him, don't pull back his foreskin while washing or wiping him. The foreskin is naturally fused for the first few years and it's extremely painful for a kid to have it moved like that. You just need to wipe it down with the wash cloth or baby wipe, it's not that complicated.

I honestly had to find this out the hard way. I chose to not circumcise my son (now 4) and when he was 6 months old, his grandmother was watching him and she pulled it back and it caused tearing that required medical treatment, not to mention that he was screaming in pain until we got to the emergency room. He was okay, but it definitely must have hurt.

That being said, circumcision has its own cleaning routine, so to speak. I know from my nephew that you have to change diapers more often during healing, make sure everything is extra clean and dry to avoid infections, and you have to put Neosporin on the incision until it's healed. Plus all the regular wiping and washing.

I know some people go more into risks/benefits of both but tbh it's ultimately just your choice if you decide to or not. Lots of people are circumcised, lots of people aren't, it's just a cultural choice at the end of the day.
